newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says China to buy more wool, cut tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Australia says China to buy more wool, cut tariffs.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Tuesday that China had agreed to buy more wool from Australia, while reducing the tariff barriers facing Australian wool exporters.

But Downer, who was briefing reporters after a meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji in Canberra, said the two had not discussed the quantity of wool to be bought or the amount of tariff reduction.
"On the wool issue, the Vice-Premier has made it clear that China will buy more wool from Australia and will begin a process of reducing its wool tariffs," Downer told reporters.
"That is, I think, very good news for wool growers in Australia and for the wool industry," Downer said.
"(But) he didn't make any commitment on an exact number."
China is Australia's largest wool export market, with sales worth A$665 million (US$512 million) in 1995/96 to June 30.
Australian wool growers have been campaigning for tariff reductions from China, the United States and India over recent months.
China currently imposes tariffs of 15 percent on wool imports, 20 percent on worsted yarn, 35 percent on worsted fabric and 37 percent on clothing.
